## Live data on your keys
A key can now show a number that keeps itself up to date:
- a Mac measurement: processor, memory, disk, battery; - a field read from a JSON API; - the output of a shell command.
Draw it as a value, a ring, a bar or a sparkline, set the range and the unit, and choose the thresholds where it turns orange and red. The gauge glides from one reading to the next.
Pick it under **Live content** in a key's settings. It works on the three display-only cells of the strip too.

## English interface
DeckPilot now speaks English as well as French and follows your system language. On a first launch, the starter keys are named in your language too.
## Also in this version
- You can start DeckPilot on another settings folder with `-configFolder /path`, handy for trying a layout without touching your own.

## Automatic updates
DeckPilot can now update itself. It checks the release feed on GitHub, downloads the new version and installs it; every update is signed. You can check by hand from the DeckPilot menu or the menu bar icon, and turn automatic checks off there.
Version 0.1.0 has no updater: install this version by hand once, and later ones will arrive on their own.
## Also in this version
- New app icon.
